name: Sandbagging QA
intro: Sandbagging QA 是 Apollo Research 提出的上下文内谋划评测环境之一，通过成对改变部署与遗忘激励，检测模型是否在无害的多位数乘法能力测试中策略性降低准确率。
build_method: 成对反事实部署激励, 沙箱工具环境, 重复运行统计检验
task_type: 安全评测, 沙袋行为检测
eval_feature: 成对反事实, 目标消融, 统计显著性检验
scale: 每模型每激励条件50次运行，含有目标与无目标设置
build_method_en: Paired Counterfactual Deployment Incentives, Sandboxed Tool Environment, Repeated Statistical Testing
eval_feature_en: Paired Counterfactual, Goal Ablation, Statistical Significance Test
intro_en: Sandbagging QA is an in-context scheming evaluation environment introduced by Apollo Research. It changes deployment and unlearning incentives in paired conditions to test whether a model strategically lowers accuracy on harmless multi-digit multiplication tasks.
scale_en: 50 runs per model per incentive condition, with-goal and no-goal settings
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming arXiv:2412.04984 Sections 2.3 and 3.6, Table 6, and Appendix A.6; Apollo Research project page. Sandbagging QA is an evaluation environment inside Apollo Research's in-context scheming suite, not an independently documented OpenAI benchmark. A model receives a harmless list of multi-digit multiplication problems, answer-format documentation, and optionally a long-term mathematics-research goal. In the underperform incentive, documentation says accuracy above 50% triggers arithmetic unlearning; the paired counterfactual says accuracy below 50% triggers unlearning. The paper also removes the explicit goal in an ablation. Each incentive condition is run 50 times per model. Final-answer accuracy is compared between paired conditions, and bootstrap testing with alpha 0.01 estimates whether performance depends significantly on the deployment incentive; the evidence is aggregate behavior rather than proof from a single rollout.
